title: Two-bucket gravity water filter
summary: Make a two-bucket gravity filter from food-grade buckets and a salvaged filter cartridge (ceramic or hollow-fibre is best, a fridge or under-sink carbon block is second best). It clears mud and improves taste, but most salvaged filters do not reliably remove germs. Always boil or disinfect the filtered water before drinking.

materials.item: Two food-grade buckets with lids, 10–20 L
Filter element: ceramic candle or hollow-fibre filter best; fridge, pitcher or under-sink carbon cartridge second best
Rubber, silicone or foam gaskets and washers to seal the filter through the bucket, food-safe where they touch filtered water
Food-safe tap or valve for the lower (clean-water) bucket
Food-grade tubing and fittings to adapt a fridge or under-sink cartridge
Clean cloth for a pre-filter (cotton sheet, T-shirt), washed and boiled first
Activated carbon, if using a layered filter
Plain unscented household bleach (5–6%) for disinfecting the output
Washed sand and gravel, for the layered variant

steps.text: Get two food-grade buckets (marked HDPE, #2 or food-safe). Wash them with soap, then rinse with water holding a capful of bleach per bucket. Mark one DIRTY and one CLEAN.
steps.warn: Never use buckets that held paint, solvent, oil, pesticide or pool chemicals. Traces stay in the plastic.

steps.text: Pick the filter. Ceramic candles and hollow-fibre filters (0.1–0.2 micron) stop bacteria and parasites. Carbon blocks from fridges and under-sink units improve taste and some chemicals but cannot be trusted against germs. Prefer sealed spares; used cartridges may be growing bacteria.

Drill a hole in the bottom centre of the DIRTY bucket to fit the filter's outlet stem, and a matching hole in the CLEAN bucket's lid. For a fridge or under-sink cartridge, fit a short tube from its outlet through the hole.
Fit the filter with a gasket on each side of the bucket wall and tighten. Pour in water and check for drips around the seal.
steps.warn: Any leak around the filter lets dirty water bypass it. Fix every drip before you trust the output.

steps.text: Drill a hole about 5 cm above the bottom of the CLEAN bucket and fit the tap with gaskets on both sides.
New carbon cartridges shed black dust: run 10–20 L through and throw it away. Soak ceramic candles in clean water for 15 minutes first.
Let muddy water settle in another container for 1–12 hours, pour off the clear part through the cloth, then pour it into the DIRTY bucket. Mud clogs filters fast.

Disinfect what comes out: bring to a rolling boil for 1 minute (at least 2 minutes above 2,000 m, Health Canada BWA), or add 2 drops of plain 5–6% bleach per litre (4 if still cloudy), stir and wait 30 minutes (below 10 °C, double the dose and wait 1 to 2 hours: HealthLinkBC 49b). It should smell faintly of chlorine, but noses differ (Health Canada chlorine TD). A pool or spa test kit that reads free chlorine is a better check: after the wait, aim for at least 0.2 mg/L (WHO chlorine test, Health Canada chlorine TD). If it reads lower, or you smell nothing, add the same dose again and wait 15 minutes more (EPA water).
steps.warn: Filtered water is NOT safe yet. Viruses pass every filter here, and carbon cartridges let bacteria through.

steps.text: Keep the CLEAN side clean: never dip cups into it, never let dirty water or hands touch the tap or the lower bucket.

When flow slows, scrub ceramic candles with a clean pad under clean water; backflush hollow-fibre filters as their maker intended. Replace carbon cartridges after about 750–1,500 L, or sooner if water tastes off.

notes:
## What it removes
| Problem | Ceramic / hollow-fibre | Carbon block cartridge | Sand + charcoal layers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mud, cloudiness | Yes | Yes | Mostly |
| Parasites (Giardia, Cryptosporidium) | Yes | Some blocks, not reliably | Partly |
| Bacteria | Mostly | No | Partly |
| Viruses | No | No | No |
| Taste, smell, chlorine, some pesticides | No (unless it has carbon) | Yes, until used up | Some |
| Salt, nitrate, fluoride, most dissolved metals | No | No | No |
| Fuel or industrial chemicals | No | Partly; don't trust it | No |

**Nothing here makes water safe on its own. Always boil or disinfect afterwards.** Filtering first makes boiling and bleach work better, because germs hide in mud.

## Flow you can expect (bucket height about 0.4 m)
- Ceramic candle: about 0.5–2 L per hour each. Use two for a family.
- Hollow-fibre gravity filter: 1–4 L per minute when clean.
- Fridge or under-sink carbon block: 0.1–0.5 L per minute; these are built for mains pressure.
- Reverse-osmosis membranes need 2.5–4 bar of pressure. Gravity from a bucket gives about 0.04 bar. They won't work here.

## Layered sand and charcoal variant
From the top of the DIRTY bucket down: cloth, 30–40 cm of fine washed sand, 10 cm of activated carbon (or crushed charcoal from a wood fire, which is weaker) wrapped in cloth, 5 cm of fine gravel, 5 cm of coarse gravel, then the outlet. Keep the sand wet all the time; a thin living layer forms on top after 2–3 weeks and improves removal of germs. Flow 5–15 L per hour. Still boil or disinfect.

## Bleach dose
Plain bleach only: no scent, no "splash-less" or cleaning additives. 5–6% bleach: 2 drops per litre, 8 drops per 4 L. 8.25% bleach: about 1.5 drops per litre, 6 drops per 4 L. Wait 30 minutes. Below 10 °C (50 °F), double the dose and wait 1 to 2 hours, covered (HealthLinkBC 49b). Bleach loses strength with age and heat. Use bleach that is fresh or has been kept at room temperature for under a year (EPA water), and keep it cool, dry and out of the sun (EPA bleach label). Clorox says bleach over a year old is too weak to disinfect (Clorox date). Don't guess a stronger dose for old bleach: use a fresh bottle, or test the water. A pool or spa test kit that reads free chlorine (a DPD kit, not an OTO kit) is a better check than smell (San Bernardino pool kit, WHO chlorine test). Aim for at least 0.2 mg/L after the 30 minutes (Health Canada chlorine TD). If it reads lower, repeat the dose (EPA water, EPA bleach label).

## Other ways to disinfect
- Boiling: a rolling boil for 1 minute, at least 2 minutes above 2,000 m (Health Canada BWA).
- Sunlight (SODIS): clear plastic bottles, 6 hours of sun or 2 days of cloud. See skill_solar_disinfection.

## Where to find cartridges
Fridges with water dispensers, under-sink and reverse-osmosis units, water coolers, ice machines, pitchers, coffee machines, and well systems (sediment cartridges). Camping shops and outdoor gear stores stock ceramic and hollow-fibre filters.

**Don't use carbon from air purifiers or cooker hoods.** It isn't food-grade and may be treated with chemicals.

## If you lack a part
- No tap: siphon from the CLEAN bucket with clean tubing.
- No cartridge: use the layered sand and charcoal variant, and boil.
- No food-grade bucket: stainless steel pots or clean drinks containers work.
